reason: The intelligent-tiering-overview quote gives up to 1,000 TPS of object restore requests per account per AWS Region from the Archive Access and Deep Archive Access tiers; the restore-options page, in the section whose quota covers S3 Intelligent-Tiering, says increased restoration limits are available through AWS Support.

Both quotes on the Intelligent-Tiering storage class page state 30 consecutive days to Infrequent Access for 40%, 90 days to Archive Instant Access for 68%, and, when turned on, 180 days to Deep Archive Access with up to 95% storage cost savings.

Quote 1 sits under the Versioning-enabled bucket bullet of the expiration considerations and states the delete marker with a unique version ID that becomes current; quote 2, for versioned buckets, states expiration applies only to the current version.

The quotes state the September 2024 default that prevents objects under 128 KB from transitioning to any storage class, the per-object transition request charge, the object size filter override, the earlier default limited to Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive, and that pre-September-2024 configurations keep it until modified.

The Lifecycle transitions row read against the header gives Yes for Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant, Flexible and Deep Archive, and No for Express One Zone, exactly as claimed.

Quote 1 states there is no expiry after initiating a multipart upload and it must be explicitly completed or stopped; quote 2 states parts can be uploaded independently, in any order, and in parallel.
The Important note states you must complete or stop the upload to stop incurring parts storage charges and only then does S3 free the parts storage and stop billing.

The decision guide definition of object storage states the unstructured format called objects, each tagged with a unique identifier and containing metadata describing the content; the claim is a near-verbatim restatement.
The What is Amazon S3 quote states each object has a key (or key name), the unique identifier for the object within the bucket.

The Object Lock page quote states prevention of delete or overwrite for a fixed or variable amount of time or indefinitely, the WORM model, and help meeting regulatory requirements that require WORM storage.

Quote 2 defines the Object writer setting (uploader owns, full control, can grant via ACLs); quote 1 states the writer account owns objects it uploads and that Object Ownership can disable ACLs so the bucket owner automatically owns every object. The claim conditions on the Object writer setting rather than on the stale by-default wording.

The quote is a bullet under You pay for all bandwidth into and out of Amazon S3, except for the following, so the first 100GB per month out to the internet, aggregated across services and Regions except China and GovCloud, is not charged.
The pricing page lists Data transferred out to Amazon CloudFront among the exceptions to paying for all bandwidth into and out of S3.
The pricing quote states per-request ingest charges for PUT, COPY or lifecycle rules into any S3 storage class and advises considering the ingest or transition cost.
The pricing quote states you pay for both the archive at the Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive rate and the temporary restored copy at the S3 Standard storage rate for a duration you choose.

The pricing quote states retrieval charges on GET for Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval, and retrieval paid as part of the restore request for Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive.

Under The meaning of public, the ACLs quote defines a public ACL by grants to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers, and the Bucket policies quote states S3 begins by assuming a policy is public, then evaluates whether it qualifies as non-public.

The FAQ answer states delete markers replicate when delete marker replication is enabled, S3 then behaves as if the object was deleted in both buckets, and replication does not support delete marker replication for tag-based rules.
Both quotes state KMS requests per second quotas apply when replicating SSE-KMS objects, covering requests you make directly and those S3 replication makes on your behalf.

The replication pricing quote states CRR adds inter-region Data Transfer OUT to each destination region, and RTC adds an RTC Data Transfer charge plus Replication Metrics billed at the CloudWatch custom metrics rate.
The requirements list states both source and destination buckets must have versioning enabled and S3 must have permissions to replicate objects to the destination bucket or buckets on your behalf.
The upload options list states that with a single PUT operation through the SDKs, REST API or CLI you can upload a single object up to 5 GB; max per single PUT matches.
The Version ID quote states S3 generates a unique version ID for each object added after versioning is enabled and objects already present have a null version ID.

The FAQ quotes state Lifecycle rules plus Versioning implement a rollback window, give the example of deleting noncurrent versions after five days with at least two newer versions, and say both numbers can be changed.
The decision guide Protocol section states block storage is high-performance, direct-attached to a compute instance with low-latency access, suited to fast and consistent I/O operations.

The decision guide Protocol section states file-based storage is natively mountable from virtually any OS using NFS and SMB and provides simple storage for shared data across multiple compute instances.

Quote 1 states content must be publicly readable to be accessed at the website endpoint for a public website; the table row under the Key difference header gives REST API endpoint both public and private, website endpoint only publicly readable.
